column1: # Language runtimes and the editor, each installed by its own version manager.
# Kept separate from tools.tsv because none of these is "download one binary".
#   name  ref   the version to install, or `stable` to track upstream on purpose
#   min   lowest version our configs work with, or `-`
#   how   which manager installs it (documentation; the step decides)
# Bump with `bs.sh update`, review the diff, then commit.
# name
nvim
nvm
node
pnpm
go
rust
# Notes on the choices above:
# nvim   lua/config/plugins/lsp.lua is written against the native vim.lsp API of
#        0.12 (see its comments about sign_define and jump.on_jump being gone),
#        so 0.11 will not do. Installed via bob, which puts it in
#        $XDG_DATA_HOME/bob/nvim-bin -- already on PATH in zsh/.zshenv.
# nvm    pinned independently of Node so two machines bootstrapped at different
#        times use the same installer behaviour.
# node   nvm, because zsh/.zshenv globs $NVM_DIR/versions/node/*/bin and reads
#        $NVM_DIR/alias/default instead of sourcing nvm.sh (~620ms saved per
#        shell). Keep `nvm alias default` in sync with this pin or that glob
#        silently picks a different version.
# go     apt's `golang-go` on resolute (26.04) is a current 1.26.x, not EOL like
#        noble's 1.22.2 was, but its patch version is Ubuntu's to pick, not
#        ours, so we still install the upstream tarball to ~/.local/go and shim
#        it into ~/.local/bin. step_go reuses an apt copy instead only when it
#        already happens to exactly match this pin.
# rust   floats on stable on purpose: nothing here depends on a rustc version,
#        clippy and rust-analyzer only get better, and re-downloading a ~200MB
#        toolchain on every bump is not worth it. `min` still catches an ancient
#        toolchain in `bs.sh doctor`.
